response: Phonorecords refer to material objects in which sounds, other than those accompanying a motion picture or other audiovisual work, are fixed by any method now known or later developed, and from which the sounds can be perceived, reproduced, or otherwise communicated, either directly or with the aid of a machine or device. These include "the material object in which the works are first fixed." According to 17 U.S.C. § 101.
